questions.question: Pipes P and Q can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 15 hours, respectively. An outlet pipe R can empty the full cistern in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together in the empty cistern, how much time will be taken to fill it completely?
questions.questionHtml: Pipes P and Q can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 15 hours, respectively. An outlet pipe R can empty the full cistern in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together in the empty cistern, how much time will be taken to fill it completely?
questions.solution:
P fills the cistern in 12 hours
Q fills the cistern in 15 hours
R empties the cistern in 20 hours

LCM of 12, 15 and 20 = 60

So, total capacity of cistern = 60 units

P’s 1 hour work = 60/12 = 5 units
Q’s 1 hour work = 60/15 = 4 units
R’s 1 hour work = -60/20 = -3 units

Net 1 hour work = 5 + 4 - 3 = 6 units

Time taken = Total work / 1 hour work
Time taken = 60/6 = 10 hours

questions.question: A right circular cone and a sphere have equal volumes. If the radius of the cone is equal to the radius of the sphere, find the ratio of the height of the cone to the radius of the sphere.
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cone and a sphere have equal volumes. If the radius of the cone is equal to the radius of the sphere, find the ratio of the height of the cone to the radius of the sphere.
questions.solution:
Volume of cone = Volume of sphere

1/3 πr²h = 4/3 πr³

Cancel 1/3, π and r²:

h = 4r

So,

h : r = 4r : r

Answer: 4 : 1

questions.question: A large cubical wooden block is to be cut into 125 smaller, identical cubical pieces. What is the minimum number of straight cuts required to achieve this?
questions.questionHtml: A large cubical wooden block is to be cut into 125 smaller, identical cubical pieces. What is the minimum number of straight cuts required to achieve this?
questions.solution:
125 = 5 × 5 × 5

So, the cube must be divided into 5 parts along each dimension.

Cuts required along one dimension = 5 - 1 = 4

Total cuts required:

4 + 4 + 4 = 12

Answer: 12 cuts

questions.solution:
Same radius, so area ratio = angle ratio

First angle = 120°
Second angle = π/3 radians = 60°

Ratio = 120 : 60

= 2 : 1

questions.question: A tangent line PQ is drawn from an external point P to a circle with center O. If the radius of the circle is 7 cm and the length of the tangent PQ is 24 cm, what is the distance from point P to the center O?
questions.questionHtml: A tangent line PQ is drawn from an external point P to a circle with center O. If the radius of the circle is 7 cm and the length of the tangent PQ is 24 cm, what is the distance from point P to the center O?
questions.solution:
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

So, OQ = 7 cm and PQ = 24 cm.

OP² = OQ² + PQ²
OP² = 7² + 24²
OP² = 49 + 576
OP² = 625
OP = 25 cm

questions.question: Find the value of k such that the quadratic equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has real and distinct roots.
questions.questionHtml: Find the value of k such that the quadratic equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has real and distinct roots.
questions.solution:
For real and distinct roots:

D > 0

k² - 4(1)(9) > 0
k² - 36 > 0
k² > 36
So, k > 6 or k < -6

From the options, only k > 6 is correct.

questions.question: In a group of students, when one student weighing 50 kg joins the group, the average weight increases by 1 kg. If another student also weighing 50 kg joins, the average weight increases by a total of 1.5 kg more than the original average. Find the original average weight of the group.
questions.questionHtml: In a group of students, when one student weighing 50 kg joins the group, the average weight increases by 1 kg. If another student also weighing 50 kg joins, the average weight increases by a total of 1.5 kg more than the original average. Find the original average weight of the group.
questions.solution:
Let original average = A and number of students = n

After 1st student joins:

50 - A = n + 1 ……(1)

After 2nd student joins, total increase = 1.5

2(50 - A) = 1.5(n + 2)

100 - 2A = 1.5n + 3
97 - 2A = 1.5n ……(2)

From (1), n = 49 - A

97 - 2A = 1.5(49 - A)
97 - 2A = 73.5 - 1.5A
23.5 = 0.5A
A = 47

questions.question: A right circular cone with a height of 24 cm is sliced parallel to its base to create a frustum. The cut is made at a height of 6 cm from the base. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone (the top part) to the volume of the frustum (the bottom part)?
questions.questionHtml: A right circular cone with a height of 24 cm is sliced parallel to its base to create a frustum. The cut is made at a height of 6 cm from the base. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller cone (the top part) to the volume of the frustum (the bottom part)?
questions.solution:
Small cone height = 24 - 6 = 18 cm

Linear ratio = 18 : 24 = 3 : 4

Volume ratio of small cone : full cone = 3³ : 4³ = 27 : 64

Frustum volume = 64 - 27 = 37

Answer: 27 : 37

questions.question: Given that √(x + 7)+ √(x - 2) = 9, find the value of x.
questions.questionHtml: Given that √(x + 7)+ √(x - 2) = 9, find the value of x.
questions.solution:
Let √(x + 7) = a and √(x - 2) = b
a + b = 9
Also, a² - b² = (x + 7) - (x - 2) = 9
(a - b)(a + b) = 9

(a - b) × 9 = 9
a - b = 1
Now, a + b = 9
a - b = 1
Adding both:
2a = 10
a = 5
So, √(x + 7) = 5
x + 7 = 25
x = 18
